prerequisites: Recommended: Prior knowledge of Radiofrequency and Microwave Technologies, Communications Electronics, Fundamentals of Telematics, Network Engineering, Network and Service Security, Telecommunication Network Management, Television and Broadcasting, Mobile Communications, Optical Communications, Electrical Energy Conversion, Testing and Verification of Electronic Equipment.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, develop and sign projects in the field of telecommunication engineering that aim at the conception and development or exploitation of telecommunication and electronic networks, services and applications.

Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation during the development of the profession of Telecommunication Technical Engineer and ease in handling specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer's activity.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunication.
To know and apply basic elements of economics and human resource management, project organization and planning, as well as legislation, regulation and standardization in telecommunications.

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary group and in a multilingual environment and to communicate, both in writing and orally, knowledge, procedures, results and ideas related to telecommunications and electronics.
Ability to autonomously learn new knowledge and techniques suitable for the conception, development or exploitation of telecommunication systems and services.

Ability to use communication and computer applications (office automation, databases, advanced calculation, project management, visualization, etc.) to support the development and exploitation of telecommunication and electronic networks, services and applications.
Ability to use computer tools for searching bibliographic resources or information related to telecommunications and electronics.

Ability to conceive, deploy, organize and manage telecommunication networks, systems, services and infrastructures in residential (home, city and digital communities), business or institutional contexts, taking responsibility for their implementation and continuous improvement, as well as knowing their economic and social impact.
Knowledge of telecommunication regulations and standards at national, European and international levels.
Know the technical characteristics of different types of telecommunication infrastructures.
Document and process the different types of projects that a Telecommunication Technical Engineer can elaborate.
Know the telecommunications regulations and standards.

syllabus_topics: Documentation, Approval, Processing and Budgeting of projects. Safety and health study.
Expert appraisal, ethical implications and legal responsibilities of the Telecommunication Engineering graduate and project management.
Broadband and telephony service distribution networks (ICT)
Sizing of Energy Generation and Storage Systems

assessment_methods.method: Part (1) - Area of Signal Theory and Communications

assessment_rules: To pass the course, each of the four parts must be passed separately. If all four parts are passed, the final grade is the weighted average: [(Grade Part (1) + Grade Part (2) + Grade Part (3)) x 0.8 / 3] + Grade Part (4) x 0.2. If any part is not passed, the final numerical grade will be the minimum of 4.5 and the weighted average calculation. For each part, the ordinary evaluation consists of a written final exam (50% of the grade, minimum 5/10 to pass the part) and continuous assessment (50% of the grade), which for parts (1), (2), and (3) includes lab practices (25%) and a building infrastructure project (25%). For part (4), continuous assessment involves activities and attendance. In the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a written final exam (50%, minimum 5/10 to pass) and an infrastructure project (50%).
